signal: Fiery launched its AI-powered FS700 Pro platform and Fiery Scribe AI in 2026, expanding its product line across manufacturers

email.body1:
Wendy, saw Fiery rolled out the AI-powered FS700 Pro platform and Fiery Scribe across new presses this year.

A product wave that broad usually means more accounts for your SDRs to work than the team can realistically follow up on, and response speed is where the best ones slip. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up on its own, so your reps spend time in conversations, not research: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I had our AI SDR draft three personalized emails to your top three target accounts off Fiery's signals. Want to hop on a quick call and I will walk you through them?
email.body2:
Wendy, quick follow-up for Fiery.

Most SDR teams lose meetings not on the first touch but on follow-up volume, ramp time, and how fast they reply when a signal fires. The manual research and CRM work eats the hours that should go to live conversations.

Worth 15 minutes? I will walk you through a teardown of your current outbound and three things I would change. Our best practices alone usually lift reply rates 50 to 70 percent.
email.body3:
Wendy, last bit of proof for Fiery.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Fiery's reply rate likely compares to similar teams. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Wendy, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.

If speeding up SDR follow-up without adding headcount is not a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Timing matters, and a big product cycle keeps everyone heads-down.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your SDR team? I will tailor it to Fiery either way.
